[ASSISTANT_SAID] Galileo's bones refer to the bones of Galileo Galilei, which were exhumed in 1737, more than 90 years after his death.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The purpose of exhuming Galileo's bones was to transfer them to a more prominent location in the Basilica of Santa Croce in Florence, Italy.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] During the exhumation, some of Galileo's bones were removed as relics and later divided among various institutions and individuals.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Two of Galileo's fingers were preserved and are now on display at the Museo Galileo in Florence.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The "square-cube law" is a mathematical principle that describes the relationship between the surface area and volume of an object as it increases in size.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The square-cube law states that as the size of an object increases, its surface area increases in proportion to the square of its size, while its volume increases in proportion to the cube of its size.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Galileo recognized the importance of the square-cube law and used it to explain why larger animals are not proportionally stronger than smaller ones.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The concepts of Galileo's bones and the square-cube law are significant in the history of science and contribute to our understanding of the natural world.  
[USER] Two figures are reciprocal when the properties of the first relative to the second are the same as those of the second relative to the first.  
[USER] Several kinds of reciprocity are known to mathematicians, and the theories of Inverse Figures and of Polar Reciprocals have been developed at great length.  
[USER] I propose to investigate a different kind of geometrical reciprocity, which is also capable of considerable development, and can be applied to the solution of mechanical problems.  
[USER] A Frame may be defined geometrically as a system of straight lines connecting a number of points.  
[USER] In actual structures, these lines are material pieces, beams, rods, or wires, and may be straight or curved; but the force by which each piece resists any alteration of the distance between the points which it joins acts in the straight line joining those points.  
[USER] When the forces acting between the two points tend to draw them together, the action along the joining line is called a Tension.  
[USER] When the forces tend to separate the points, the action along the joining line is called a Pressure.
